about.title: San Luis Obispo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Luis Obispo's mix of commuter traffic and campus-area driving means collisions happen at predictable spots and times, including Friday afternoon slowdowns near Los Osos Valley Road and the US-101 southbound stretch. Public records show 179 injury collisions and 223 people injured over the most recent full year, a reminder that even a routine drive through downtown or along Higuera Street can turn into something that upends your week or your finances. If you were hurt, the period right after a crash matters: insurers move fast, memories fade, and physical evidence like skid marks or vehicle damage can disappear. We handle car accident cases in the San Luis Obispo area and can review your claim at no cost. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee owed unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What to Understand Before You Talk to an Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: Most car accident claims in California must be filed within two years, but if a government entity (like a city road department) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Missing either deadline can end your ability to recover anything.

items.title: Pure Comparative Fault Still Allows Recovery
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the crash, with your share of fault reducing (not eliminating) your compensation. Insurers often try to shift blame early, so it helps to have someone reviewing the details before you accept their version of events.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. That makes it especially important to document how the crash has actually affected your daily life, not just your medical bills.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since insurers often use those statements to minimize what they owe. You're not required to provide one right away, and we can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on US-101 or another state highway?
items.answer: Crashes on state highways like the US-101 southbound corridor can sometimes involve government agencies such as Caltrans, which may trigger a much shorter claims deadline, sometimes just six months. It's worth having us evaluate this quickly rather than waiting.
